content:
在此订阅：Apple 播客 | Spotify | YouTube |阴天 | Pocket Casts 就这样，黄仁勋又回到了巅峰。据报道，特朗普总统致电英伟达董事会，鼓励其恢复两周前被赶下台的前首席执行官的职位。特朗普在《Truth Social》上写道，董事会做出了“正确且恰当的决定”，这确保了“不仅是公司的成功和繁荣，也是美国经济的成功和繁荣。”总统看上去很高兴。技术领导者松了口气。股市似乎因这一消息而上涨。然而，许多其他感兴趣的各方仍然存在紧迫的问题。两党议员正计划盘问黄与一名疑似中国间谍的恋情以及相关的国家安全威胁。但刚刚强烈投票反对人工智能、数据中心和富人之间的欺诈行为的美国人将如何接受总统向他的科技首席执行官朋友放行呢？在大西洋广播电台的这一集中，查理·沃泽尔谈论了英伟达、黄仁勋、科技首席执行官的短期思维以及被人工智能劫持的经济。以下是该集的文字记录： 查理·沃泽尔：我们刚刚举行了一次选举，正如您提到的，美国对人工智能和数据中心表示了深切关注，数据中心是所有英伟达芯片的所在地。
一群新的立法者带着美国的授权来到这里，试图控制这个，比如，科技精英阶层，这个人们觉得类似于人质情况的人工智能经济，对吧？你会在华盛顿特区发生所有这些冲突，我认为这将是一场噩梦。我真的这么做。 [音乐] Hanna Rosin：今天，黄仁勋恢复担任芯片制造巨头英伟达董事长。埃隆·马斯克在 X 上发帖称，“错误已被纠正。”总统称这是“正确且恰当的决定”，并发布了一条人工智能生成的表情包，显示黄的举起拳头的姿势与特朗普本人在 2024 年宾夕法尼亚州巴特勒刺杀事件后采取的姿势相同。因此，对于总统、黄仁勋和其他科技巨头来说：秩序已恢复。但对于很多其他人来说——什么？我是汉娜·罗辛。这是大西洋广播电台。距离与总统关系密切的黄承认与一名疑似中国间谍有染仅两周时间。此时此刻，国会领导人仍在继续传唤黄先生就他的事件对国家安全构成的危险作证。与中国围绕间谍活动、人工智能主导地位的摊牌仍然是我们这个时代迫在眉睫的威胁。然而，黄就在他角落的办公室里，穿着他最新的皮夹克。与我一起讨论的是科技作家兼 Galaxy Brain 播客主持人 Charlie Warzel。查理，我们再次在这里谈论这个永不停息的故事。
欢迎来到这个节目。 Warzel：谢谢你邀请我。我两周前就告诉过你这是噩梦般的场景，而我们现在正处于噩梦之中。罗辛：我知道这是我的第一个问题。所以，当你今天早上醒来得知黄仁勋重返 Nvidia 的消息时，你是否认为，不可能？或者我知道这会发生。我告诉过你了？沃泽尔：老实说，介于两者之间。周日，[财政部长]斯科特·贝森特开始退缩了一些。他参加了——我相信是哥伦比亚广播公司——的一个早间节目，他最初采取了非常强硬的立场，即英伟达董事会需要在公司外部寻找领导力。

【原文 English Original】
Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts Just like that, Jensen Huang is back on top. Reportedly, President Trump called Nvidia’s board and encouraged it to reinstate the former CEO, who had been pushed out only two weeks earlier. The board made the “correct and proper decision,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, which ensures the “Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.” The president seemed happy. Tech leaders were relieved. The stock market seemed to rally with the news. A lot of other interested parties, however, still have burning questions. Lawmakers from both parties are planning to grill Huang about the affair he had with a suspected Chinese spy and the related threats to national security. But how will Americans, who just voted resoundingly against AI, data centers, and grift among the rich, receive the president giving a pass to his tech-CEO friend? On this episode of Radio Atlantic , Charlie Warzel talks about Nvidia, Huang, the short-term thinking of tech CEOs, and an economy held hostage by AI. The following is a transcript of the episode: Charlie Warzel: We just had an election where, as you alluded to, America expressed deep concern with artificial intelligence in general, with data centers, which are the thing that house all the Nvidia chips. And you have a class of new lawmakers who are coming in with a mandate from America to try to rein in this, like, tech-elite class, this AI economy that people feel is akin to a hostage situation, right? You’re gonna have, like, all of that collide in D.C., and I think it’s gonna be a nightmare. I really do. [ Music ] Hanna Rosin: Today, Jensen Huang was reinstated as chairman of Nvidia, the chip-manufacturing giant. Elon Musk posted on X, “The mistake has been corrected.” The president referred to it as the “correct and proper decision” and posted an AI-generated meme showing Huang in the same raised-fist pose that Trump himself adopted after the 2024 assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania. So for the president, for Huang, and for other tech giants: order restored. For a lot of other people, though—what? I’m Hanna Rosin. This is Radio Atlantic . It’s been just about two weeks since Huang, who is close to the president, admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Congressional leaders are at this very moment continuing to call up Huang to testify about the dangers his affair posed to national security. The showdown with China over spying, over AI dominance, is still a looming threat of our era. And yet, there is Huang, right back in his corner office with his latest leather jacket. Joining me to discuss is tech writer and host of the Galaxy Brain podcast Charlie Warzel. Charlie, we are here once again talking about the story that never stops giving. Welcome to the show. Warzel: Thank you for having me. I told you this is the nightmare scenario two weeks ago, and here we are in the nightmare. Rosin: I knew that was my first question. So when you woke up this morning to the news that Huang was reinstated at Nvidia, do you think, No way ? Or I knew this was gonna happen. I told you so ? Warzel: Somewhere in between, honestly. It was starting to get—on Sunday, [Treasury Secretary] Scott Bessent sort of walked back a little bit. He was on—I believe on CBS—one of the morning shows, and he initially took this very strident position that the Nvidia board needed to look outside the company for leadership. And then when pressed on it again, he kind of backtracked and said, Well, you know, Jensen Huang is actually now on the outside . And so that signaled a little to me that this week could get a little crazy. I didn’t anticipate it happening this quickly, though. Rosin: I mean, there has been a lot of reporting that President Trump was involved in the decision, that he called into the Nvidia board meeting to advocate for the return of Huang. What do we know so far about the president’s involvement? Warzel: I mean, this is—I don’t know if it’s unprecedented. But this is a lot of involvement from the president of the United States in a publicly traded company’s personnel decisions to—he said he both intervened directly and indirectly, whatever indirectly means. But there were calls, supposedly. There have been communications over the recent weeks with Trump and Jensen Huang, who are cellphone buddies. It’s remarkable. The hedge-fund manager Bill Ackman said that the wisdom of the crowd has spoken , which I think is a very odd way to describe the president of the United States intervening in the workings of a corporate board. But hey, the wisdom of a crowd has spoken, I guess. Rosin: Okay, so what we know so far is that the president was probably heavily involved in the decision to return back to the top of this company someone who was implicated in a national-security scandal. So it’s not obvious why a president would intervene in that way. So let’s unpack it a little bit. One theory why Trump would intervene in this way is the economy, right? Warzel: So there’s a lot here. As we talked about on a previous episode of this, as a lot of people, including myself, have written about and reported on: Nvidia, in some ways, can be seen as, like, a load-bearing block of the global economy, right? They both power the AI boom with their chips. They also invest into the AI companies through this, like, five-layer cake that Jensen Huang helped create, the circular financing, right? So they both power the boom; they finance the boom. That makes them very critical to the global economy. There are a lot of people who argue that Jensen Huang essentially, like, is the one man whose fate determines whether the market goes up and down. Nvidia stock for a while was down, but the rest of the economy was doing okay. It was kind of shouldering this. And then late last week, there was a pretty big sell-off led by a lot of tech stocks. And a lot of the year’s gains in the S&P 500 were lost. So people were kind of freaking out. I think it’s also no coincidence that this was announced—Huang’s reinstatement came—just, you know, right before the markets opened on Monday, after this huge sell-off on Friday. So the economy is a big part of this. Donald Trump believes, according to all the reporting that we’ve seen, that Jensen Huang is a critical part of the AI boom, which is, you know, propping up the rest of the stock market. Rosin: So it’s not just that Nvidia is too big to fail. It’s too much of a risk. It’s Jensen Huang, specifically? Warzel: That’s the belief. I mean, that’s at least what a lot of these tech leaders are saying too. So there’s really, like, three cohorts that have been agitating for this. One is Nvidia shareholders, who, obviously, Jensen Huang has made them tons and tons of money, especially if you’ve been a shareholder for a very long time in the company. But even anyone who got in after the ChatGPT revolution has seen huge gains, a stock split. So they want this guy back because he’s made them a lot of money. Then you have the Silicon Valley–elite class. I would argue the Silicon Valley–elite class wants this because they want the AI boom to continue. They have a lot riding on this. All the AI CEOs have a whole bunch of investments of their own that are predicated on all the numbers going up and up and up. But also, I think, there’s a cultural reason for this, which is: They do not want to see arguably the greatest visionary, the most irreplaceable CEO in Silicon Valley ousted, because it means that they could be ousted. It means that the CEO is vulnerable, that the visionary founder is vulnerable. I think that’s, like, a very big part of this. This is one of the existential crises that these guys have been going through, because everyone thought that Jensen was too big to fail. The fact that he had to resign after all this pressure and the board didn’t want him back is, I think to them, a very, very scary proposition because it means they can no longer act with impunity. So that was one of the reasons. And then I think you have Donald Trump, who wanted the economy to keep going on his watch, and this was the thing, the lever he thought he could pull to make number go up. Rosin: So it’s like there’s a Silicon Valley myth of a genius, and Trump has used the word genius recently. And that’s a cultural trope, but it’s also real because it drives the stock market. So it’s kind of a circular logic around this word visionary and genius that you just mentioned. Warzel: Yeah, I mean, I think that so much of stock markets, it’s a confidence game. And I don’t mean that in the sense of: It’s a con. I mean, it’s about having confidence in the market, having confidence in the direction of things. For so long, we have been talking about the economy as being propped up by AI, and we’ve been talking about AI in America as having all this very peculiar circular financing, about Is this a bubble? Is this not a bubble? And there’s this idea around all of it of extreme precarity, right? That all of this is contingent on a big bet that has been made, both about the technology succeeding but also about all of this different type of financing and all this historic investment actually meaning something and going somewhere. You need confidence from all of these investors, from all of these folks. Jensen Huang is somebody who, for this class of people, projected a lot of confidence and instilled a lot of confidence in the direction of where the economy and where the AI boom is going. So with him out of it, there was a lot of uncertainty. We were starting to see that in the markets. This freaked a lot of people out. Rosin: Right, and they don’t like uncertainty. Okay, let me run another Trump motivation by you. Lately, Trump has been talking about Alice Huang—the woman who Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with and who U.S. intelligence officials are suspecting to be a spy—has been sort of diminishing her role. He said recently, “Every time you have a Chinese woman that’s good-looking or beautiful, they say she’s a spy.” Now we’ve heard this from the president, not from U.S. intelligence officials. And I was wondering if there’s something in here about Trump minimizing affairs because of his own history, sort of minimizing the importance of this kind of scandal taking down a great leader. Warzel: I think it’s not only just Trump; it’s all these folks we’re talking about in Silicon Valley. They’ve all been approaching this scandal not from the geopolitical angle of this, but from the moral-infidelity angle, right? Saying, you know, Everyone has their foibles; everyone is flawed; geniuses can be flawed too. Everyone deserves a second chance . And it’s really not a question about morality. There’s obviously, you know, the corporate-HR level of things, which is that there’s been reporting about Huang having affairs with employees in the company, including a direct report. Alice Huang was also a client of Nvidia’s, of Jensen Huang, so there’s an impropriety there. But that’s not the thing that people, that lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are upset about right now. They’re upset about the fact that Alice Huang has this alleged tie to Chinese intelligence, and what, if anything, this did to the larger geopolitical question: whether Megaspeed, this company she worked with, was skirting U.S. chip-export bans, allowing Nvidia chips to get into China or to be used by China in these remote-access data centers; or whether or not Alice Huang was reporting on things that Jensen Huang was doing; whether she had access to any of his devices or anything like that—all of those geopolitical concerns. So it’s interesting to watch both Trump and all these executives sort of not talk about that, and just focus on this other morality play. But I think what we know is actually very troubling. There’s good evidence to suggest that a lot of chip-smuggling was going on. We don’t know whether Huang and Nvidia were directly related to this, but we know that Megaspeed certainly had some role to play in this ecosystem. And Megaspeed, it should be said, has declined all allegations of wrongdoing here. And The New York Times reported on Sunday that Alice Huang had been keeping in touch with an agent in the Chinese intelligence service for over a year. She’d been speaking with this person and staying in contact with them while she was maintaining this relationship with Jensen Huang. So that’s a lot of time. And it’s very interesting to see that report come out on Sunday and have him get reinstated on Monday. [ Music ] Rosin: When we come back, we talk about how this is more than just an economic story. [ Break ] Rosin: So right now, at this moment, there are two camps. There’s the President Trump–Jensen Huang tech-leader camp. They want Jensen Huang to come back. But the other track, which is the national-security track, is continuing to move forward. Congressional leaders are still asking Jensen Huang to come and testify. And polls show that Americans actually do care about the national-security risks involved here. So presumably, the story—you and I are gonna be talking about this again. This story is not going to go away. Let’s take the congressional testimonies first. What does it look like if you have Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, testifying before Congress with the president’s backing—as opposed to what could have been, which is Jensen Huang, a citizen, not beholden to the company, not the CEO, and without the support of the president? Warzel: In an interesting way, this is just a way bigger scandal now. Like, this is a way bigger, thornier, more intense, more interesting scandal. Which, again, if you’re Donald Trump—and, also, people who care about, you know, Nvidia’s relationship to the global economy and the AI boom—the logic doesn’t fully make sense there, right? You would probably want this to go away rather than become, like, the central story of Washington, D.C., for the next 12 months or so. It remains to be seen whether Huang will just come there and plead the Fifth, right? Just say, like, absolutely nothing because basically anything he could say seems like it may or may not jeopardize Nvidia’s position, a bunch of other people. He is now in charge of this company. It’s also going to absolutely invigorate the investigations, again, which you’re seeing are coming from both China hawks or just people who are very upset about the way that this has been handled by the Trump administration and Trump’s involvement in getting him reinstated. I sort of don’t have words for how charged this is going to be. We just had an election where, as you alluded to, America expressed deep concern with artificial intelligence in general, with data centers, which are the thing that house all the Nvidia chips. And you have a class of new lawmakers who are coming in with a mandate from America to try to rein in this, like, tech-elite class, this AI economy that people feel is akin to a hostage situation, right? You have all of these people saying, If you don’t let us build what we wanna do and act the way that we wanna do, then the numbers gonna go down. All this, you know—the bubble’s gonna pop, and good luck, right? Nice economy you got there; hope nothing happens to it , sort of situation. You’re gonna have, like, all of that collide in D.C., and I think it’s gonna be a nightmare. I really do. Rosin: Yeah, that’s absolutely correct because if there is one desire from this midterm flip, it’s accountability. Like, let us enter an era of accountability where rich people don’t get to get away with whatever they want to get away with. That’s what the people seem to be asking for, both in their concerns about corruption, their concerns about data centers, everything that you just mentioned. And this just feels like a sort of pushback to all that. Warzel: Absolutely. And I think that a lot of people are gonna have stuff to prove here, right? They’re gonna wanna make an example out of all of this. And I was talking to somebody in Silicon Valley this morning about this, and they were saying to me that the election really showed this really short-term political thinking, right? The tech leaders were so focused on the AI bet that they allowed themselves to get caught up in, you know, hitching their wagon to Trump and the MAGA situation, right? Like, all the donations for the ballroom, the standing behind him at the inauguration, all of the meetings, the fawning, and all of that. And not seeing that the political winds could blow, you know, in other directions, that hitching your star to this guy so completely was a bad calculation. It’s because they had this short-term thinking. And this person described this to me as, like, another perfect example of the short-term thinking. Like, yes, we solved this problem in the very near term. The stock market is gonna rally now on all of this. But what’s it gonna mean for this to become a far bigger political scandal? Like, what is that going to mean potentially to, you know, how the Democrats are going to position themselves against AI in 2028? Like, it seems like they are playing checkers instead of, you know, the seven-dimensional chess that they always claim to be playing. Rosin: Yeah. Well, Charlie, it looks like there’s gonna be a showdown, and I look forward to talking to you about it when it unfolds. Thank you so much for explaining this to us. Warzel: Yeah. Absolutely. Happy to be here. Rosin: That is all for today’s show. [ Music ] Rosin: This episode of Radio Atlantic was produced by Mike Pesoli and edited by Hadley Robinson. It was engineered by Miguel Carrascal and has original music by Rob Smierciak. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of podcasts, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor. If you like what you saw here today, new episodes of Radio Atlantic drop every Monday and Thursday. You can find them on The Atlantic ’s YouTube page. You can find them on Apple or Spotify or wherever it is you get your podcasts. And you can subscribe to this publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. Until next time, I’m Hanna Rosin.

content:
本月的 11 天里，硅谷给人的印象是，尽管困难重重，它最终还是要经历真正的耻辱时刻。首先，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋承认，他与一名涉嫌间谍的中国女商人欺骗了他的妻子，这让他的公司、它所支撑的人工智能行业以及国家安全面临风险。他深表歉意。随后有报道称，黄仁勋还与英伟达的一名高管有染，随后他辞职了。硅谷的一位巨头似乎正面临清算。但昨晚深夜，唐纳德·特朗普在 Truth Social 上发帖称，“我希望英伟达董事会重新聘用黄仁勋。”总统写道，这一结果“对于公司以及美国来说都是最好的事情”。这句话显然既是命令，又是愿望。今天上午，英伟达董事会宣布一致投票决定恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官。总统随后发布了一个表情包，即使对他来说也是怪诞的：一张看似人工智能生成的黄的图像，脸上受伤流血，举起拳头握紧红色胸罩，背景中飘扬着英伟达的旗帜——当然，这是模仿特朗普第一次暗杀企图后不久拍摄的照片。真是太羞耻了。 [阅读：A] 价值 5.7 万亿美元的面部植物 值得强调的是黄的丑闻有多么严重。
他承认与一名中国女商人有关系，该女商人涉嫌将英伟达芯片走私到中国，从而规避美国的出口管制，同时他还在不知疲倦地游说放松限制，以防止美国芯片落入中国竞争者之手。对于像英伟达这样的公司来说，这是一个惊天动地的启示：英伟达基本上垄断了用于训练最先进人工智能模型的芯片。这使得该公司变得异常富有——今年早些时候，其估值达到创纪录的 5.7 万亿美元。反过来，黄仁勋利用这笔财富来支持人工智能经济的大部分，为各种数据中心和初创企业提供资金，作为一种财务支持。黄先生辞职后，华尔街经历了近期记忆中最糟糕的一周之一。自他辞职以来，有关第三次婚外情和滥用管理风格的进一步报道只会让黄的处境变得更糟。几乎任何其他行业发生类似丑闻都会导致普遍的政治谴责，并且该公司及其同行都试图与这位名誉扫地的前高管保持距离。但这里恰恰相反。据《纽约时报》报道，特朗普和副总统万斯周末敦促英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋的职位。
今天早上宣布这一消息后，特朗普几乎立即在《真相社交》上发帖，庆祝恢复“伟大爱国者和国宝”黄蜂的“正确和恰当”决定。硅谷的气氛十分热烈：消息传出后，该公司股价上涨了 30% 以上，投资者和科技高管爆发出热烈的掌声。对冲基金经理比尔·阿克曼 (Bill Ackman) 在 X 上写道：“大众的智慧占了上风。”黄的直言不讳的支持者埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 补充道：“错误已被纠正。”硅谷许多最有权势的人物似乎都被证明是正确的——毕竟，他们淡化并认为黄的愚蠢行为只是简单的错误和失常。事实上，整个事情——鲁莽和丑闻以及随后的有罪不罚——是科技界的常态。硅谷

【原文 English Original】
For 11 days this month, Silicon Valley gave the impression that it would finally, against all odds, subject itself to a genuine moment of shame. First, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having cheated on his wife with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being a spy, putting his company, the AI industry it undergirds, and the nation’s security at risk. He apologized profusely. Then it was reported that Huang had had another affair, this one with an Nvidia executive, and he resigned. It seemed that one of Silicon Valley’s titans was facing a reckoning. But late last night, Donald Trump posted on Truth Social, “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang.” This outcome, the president wrote , “would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.” Those words were evidently as much a command as they were a wish. This morning, Nvidia’s board of directors announced that it had unanimously voted to reinstate Huang as CEO. The president then posted a meme that, even for him, was grotesque: a seemingly AI-generated image of Huang, face bloodied from a wound, raising a fist clenching a red brassiere with an Nvidia flag waving in the background—modeled, of course, on the photo taken just after the first assassination attempt on Trump. So much for shame. [ Read:A ] $5.7 Trillion Face-Plant It’s worth underscoring just how damning Huang’s scandals were. He admitted to having a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman tied to a company that was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China—thereby sidestepping U.S. export controls—at the same time that he was lobbying tirelessly to ease restrictions meant to keep American chips out of the hands of Chinese competition. For a company in Nvidia’s position, it was an earth-shattering revelation: Nvidia essentially has a monopoly on the chips used to train the most advanced AI models. That has made the firm spectacularly wealthy—earlier this year, it was valued at a record $5.7 trillion. Huang, in turn, used that wealth to underwrite much of the AI economy, funding all manner of data centers and start-ups as a sort of financial backstop. Huang’s resignation was followed by one of the worst weeks on Wall Street in recent memory. Further reports since his resignation—of a third affair and an abusive management style—only made Huang come off worse. A similar scandal in almost any other industry would result in universal political condemnation and an attempt, by both the company and its peers, to distance themselves from the disgraced former executive. But it’s just the opposite here. The New York Times has reported that Trump and Vice President Vance spent the weekend pushing Nvidia’s board to reinstate Huang. Almost immediately after this morning’s announcement, Trump posted on Truth Social to celebrate “the correct and proper” decision to restore Huang, a “Great Patriot and National Treasure.” The mood in Silicon Valley is ebullient: The company’s stock jumped by more than 30 percent on the news, and investors and tech executives have erupted in an ovation. “The wisdom of the crowd prevails,” the hedge-fund manager Bill Ackman wrote on X. Elon Musk, a vocal Huang supporter, added : “The mistake has been corrected.” Many of Silicon Valley’s most powerful characters seem vindicated—after all, they downplayed and dismissed Huang’s follies as simple mistakes and aberrations. In fact, the whole thing—recklessness and scandal followed by impunity—is the norm in the tech world. Silicon Valley has developed a reputation for generosity and forgiveness when it comes to its own sins. Musk has appeared to endorse racist and xenophobic conspiracy theories but sits on a multitrillion-dollar empire of businesses. Meta has been credibly accused of fueling ethnic violence, enabling the spread of misinformation, and harming children through addictive product design—the latter for which it agreed to a major settlement this summer—but remains among the largest companies in the world, and is structured such that Mark Zuckerberg basically cannot be fired. Almost exactly three years ago, Sam Altman was fired from OpenAI for being “not consistently candid” with the firm’s board of directors, only to be reinstated within days after Microsoft and other major investors rallied behind him. Now the entire AI industry is rushing headlong to build products that are jeopardizing the internet as we know it and, per AI executives’ own warnings, could destroy the planet. Meanwhile, Anthropic employees, post–public offering, are estimated to be worth more than the bottom third of U.S. households. Over the past week and a half, legions of tech CEOs came out in support of Huang. “America needs to have more Jensens,” Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas said last Monday. This morning, the investor Chamath Palihapitiya wrote on X that Nvidia’s decision “prevented a massive economic own goal.” Just business as usual for some of the wealthiest companies in the world. (Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.) Altman, asked last week about whether he thought Huang should return, demurred but said he felt “personal strong empathy” for his (soon-to-be) fellow ex-ex-CEO. This morning, Altman posted a single word: “Jensen!” Huang’s return underscores the most important and perhaps singular value driving Silicon Valley: winning. Today that means more chips and data centers, more powerful AI models, greater revenues, soaring stock prices and valuations. Integrity, candor, atonement, and consequences seem like secondary concerns. The repercussions of the industry’s failures—wild swings in the stock market, technologies that wreak havoc on other industries and individual lives, a corrosion of cultural decency—are for everyone else to manage. Personal victory also happens to be one of the president’s major motivations. Trump has aligned himself with every tech CEO he deems successful—Altman, Apple’s Tim Cook, and most of all Huang, who is once again arguably the most influential CEO in the world. Earlier this year, in a now infamous interview, Huang said that “you’re not talking to somebody who woke up a loser.” Today, Silicon Valley decided to embrace its once and future king, whatever mistakes he made. After just 11 days of losing, Huang woke up winning once again.

content:
更新于下午 6:06美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 23 日美国人在过去几天学到了一些东西。最新消息是，黄仁勋在因与一名据称与中国情报机构有关的女性发生婚外情而遭受一纳秒的耻辱后，又重新控制了英伟达，这家制造世界上最先进人工智能芯片的巨头公司。另一个原因是中国共产党政权已经掌握了芯片。像往常一样，市场再次确认他们更喜欢利润而不是政治：黄仁勋回归的消息传出后，英伟达的股价上涨了 30% 以上。但最重要的是，美国人再次认识到他们的总统并不关心美国的国家安全。事实上，他如此强烈地抵制任何安全概念，以至于他的行为几乎与敌对外国特工的行为没有区别。退后一步，考虑一下这一系列事件。这位已婚的英伟达老板被发现与一位名叫爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)的女子发生性关系。 （她与 Jensen 没有关系，但我在这里会使用名字以避免混淆。）Alice 在这起事件中为新加坡的 Megaspeed 公司工作。 Megaspeed 购买了 Nvidia 芯片，然后不顾美国的出口管制，想方设法将其运往中国。据报道，她在与詹森交往的同时，还与中国情报机构国家安全部保持着联系。
（一些报道称爱丽丝为“特工”或“间谍”，另一些则称她为“资产”。这种区别在詹森的案例中没有什么实际区别。受雇于情报机构、接受过专业培训、可能以虚假身份行事的人就是一名官员。特工和资产是从组织外部的私人生活中招募的人，他们与这样的机构有不同程度的合作关系，但实际上并没有被雇佣为间谍。无论如何，詹森实际上是一名官员。与据报道与中国情报人员上床的人上床。） [乔什·泰兰吉尔：黄仁勋复活的三种理论] 所有这一切看起来确实很糟糕。情况变得更糟。美国情报部门警告包括特朗普总统在内的美国政府，爱丽丝与北京有纠葛。事实上，特朗普在七个月内两次收到警告，其中一次是在五月份特朗普前往中国进行国事访问时，马可·卢比奥在空军一号上发表简报时发出的。这肯定很尴尬，因为不久之后，黄仁勋登上了空军一号，与美国代表团一起开始了中国之行。特朗普忽视了这些警告——或者更准确地说，以典型的特朗普风格，他假装不知道这些问题。 “我当然会向情报人员核实，”他在最近一次访问中国之前说道。 “他们本可以被提及。当然，这对我影响不大。”显然不是。
这些警告也没有打动商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克，他的前公司 Cantor Fitzgerald 与英伟达有着密切的联系，包括为一些购买其芯片的公司提供资金。该公司现在由卢特尼克的儿子经营。特朗普对这一切有何反应？当詹森被发现并不得不离开他的公司时，特朗普立即开始工作，试图让他重新坐回英伟达的大椅子上。 “我很高兴看到詹森获得第二次机会。你知道，我们是一个充满第二次机会的国家。”英伟达没有这样做：该公司的内部消息人士明确表示

【原文 English Original】
Updated at 6:06 p.m. ET on November 23, 2026 Americans learned several things over the past few days. The most recent news is that Jensen Huang, after a nanosecond of disgrace for an affair with a woman allegedly connected to Chinese intelligence , is back in control of Nvidia, the giant corporation that makes some of the world’s most advanced AI chips. Another is that China’s Communist regime has gotten its hands on the chips. The markets, as usual, have reconfirmed that they prefer profit to politics: Nvidia’s stock price jumped more than 30 percent on the news of Huang’s return. But most important, Americans learned—yet again—that their president does not care about the national security of the United States. In fact, he is so aggressively resistant to any notion of security that his actions have become almost indistinguishable from those of a hostile foreign agent. Step back for a moment and consider this sequence of events. The married Nvidia boss was caught in a sexual relationship with a woman named Alice Huang. (She is not related to Jensen, but I will use first names here to avoid confusion.) Alice, during this affair, worked for Megaspeed, a company in Singapore. Megaspeed bought Nvidia chips, and then found ways to get them to China, despite U.S. export controls. She also reportedly maintained contacts with the Ministry of State Security, the Chinese intelligence agency, while carrying on with Jensen. (Some reports call Alice an “agent” or a “spy,” others refer to her as an “asset.” The distinction makes little practical difference in Jensen’s case. Someone who is employed by an intelligence agency, has professional training, and may be acting under a false identity, is an officer . Agents and assets are people recruited from private life, outside of the organization, who have a cooperative relationship, in varying degrees, with such an agency but aren’t actually employed as spooks. Either way, Jensen was literally in bed with someone who was reportedly in bed with Chinese intelligence.) [ Josh Tyrangiel: Three theories of Jensen Huang’s resurrection ] All of this certainly looks bad. It gets worse. The United States government, including President Trump, was warned by American intelligence that Alice was entangled with Beijing. In fact, Trump was warned twice in seven months, including once during a briefing by Marco Rubio aboard Air Force One in May as Trump was headed to China for a state visit. This must have been awkward, because shortly afterward, Jensen Huang boarded Air Force One and joined the U.S. delegation for the trip to China. Trump ignored these warnings—or more accurately, in classic Trump style, he pretended not to know about these issues. “I’d certainly check with the intelligence people,” he said, just before his most recent visit to China. “They could have been mentioned. Certainly, it didn’t make much of an impact on me.” Clearly not. Nor did these warnings move Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, whose former company, Cantor Fitzgerald, has significant ties to Nvidia , including financing some of the firms that were buying its chips. The company is now run by Lutnick’s son. Trump’s reaction to all this? When Jensen was discovered and had to leave his company, Trump got right to work trying to put him back in the big chair at Nvidia. “I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance. You know, we’re a country of second chances.” Nvidia wasn’t having it : Internal sources at the company made clear to reporters that Jensen Huang would not be reinstated. So what changed in a matter of days? Nothing, except that the president apparently brought the American intelligence community into the fray to give Jensen a clean bill of health. At least that’s how it sounds from the Nvidia board’s public statement: “In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” The national-security process is slow and deliberative for a reason; people with even modest clearances who have been accused of minor infractions have had to wait months, sometimes even going to court, before being allowed back to work. An executive working with some of America’s most exotic technology commits adultery with a foreign citizen who has ties to a hostile government, and is credibly accused of funneling highly restricted American technology to a hostile intelligence service—and the U.S. security mandarins give the guy a thumbs-up after a week ? Trump likes Jensen, he likes money, he likes the markets, and he likes Lutnick and his family. So perhaps he told the American spooks to sound the all-clear so that Jensen could get back to work. Trump indicated as much today when he told CNBC that he spoke with Nvidia’s board members. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way. And I convinced them.” In a statement on Truth Social, Trump said: “The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” That means exactly nothing. Saying that Todd Blanche does not “possess evidence” is an artful formulation meaning that Blanche does not have a file in front of him from the intelligence community detailing Jensen’s acts, some of which might have been dangerous even if they were not “unlawful.” (As any government employee can tell you, any number of “lawful” activities, including carrying lots of debt or having emotional problems, can sink a clearance and a job.) And because of Trump’s pressure to clear Jensen, it’s unlikely he ever will. Not only did Trump celebrate the Nvidia decision, but he noted that the board’s action possibly averted a worse outcome: Jensen Huang working for China. If Jensen was “mad” enough, Trump said during an interview today , he might have accepted an offer to lead a Chinese company, because the Nvidia boss has some of their “blood in him.” In other words, the United States just vouched for a man the president said might have defected to China if he hadn’t been given his job back. [ Jonathan Chait: Trump’s backing of Huang is not superintelligent ] To recap: After a top industrialist got caught in an affair with a woman who might have been using the affair to slip American technology to a U.S. enemy, the president declared that his own spies had cleared his pal, waved off the national-security damage, and left everyone, ostensibly, happy. And by “everyone,” I mean Jensen Huang, Howard Lutnick, Nvidia stockholders, and Communist China. Trump solved this problem in a way that would make a foreign spy or a lobbyist for a foreign government both impressed and envious. Enemy spooks, their agents, and their assets spend their lives trying to do what Trump did in a week. Jensen’s off the hook, and the stock has bounced back. (And the Chinese should give Alice a medal.) This whole terrible situation shows in galling detail that Trump just doesn’t think very much about the interests of the United States. (It also suggests that he couldn’t care less about the recent election, in which corruption was a top issue for many voters.) He makes no secret of his preference for his own relationships over America’s safety: When asked if Russian President Vladimir Putin was a “friend to America,” Trump shrugged and said, “I can’t speak to America. ” That’s because Trump, for all his flag-hugging nonsense, doesn’t think in terms of “America” or “China” or “Russia.” He is a globalist, in the very worst sense of the word: a man who cares nothing for states or peoples or ideologies, because he sees the world as just an interconnected group of companies and banks. Some of those companies are run by his friends, and those are the only peers who matter. Everyone else is just raw material or collateral damage; the masses are just ciphers who either obey him or obey someone else. It is perhaps an insult to foreign agents to say that Trump is acting like them. Foreign agents work for countries, and care about them. They do what they do out of patriotism, however misguided they may be about the regimes they might serve. Trump has no such ideals. Trump’s business is Trump’s business, and everything else—including “national interest” and “national security”—are just meaningless phrases used by chumps and saps. This article was updated to clarify the words agent , officer , and asset .

title: Why Trump Rescued Jensen Huang
zh_title: 特朗普为何拯救黄仁勋
summary: 一个按照正常道德规则甚至自我保护来运作的总统将忙于与英伟达丑闻的影响保持距离。昨晚，《纽约时报》报道称，一名与英伟达曾经和未来的首席执行官黄仁勋有染的中国女子与中国间谍机构经常保持联系。这位名叫爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）的女士可能影响了英伟达首席执行官将先进芯片出售给将其转移到中国的公司的决定。唐纳德·特朗普反而推动恢复黄仁勋担任公司首席执行官，甚至甚至拨通了电话。
content:
一个按照正常道德规则甚至自我保护来运作的总统将忙于与英伟达丑闻的影响保持距离。昨晚，《纽约时报》报道称，一名与英伟达曾经和未来的首席执行官黄仁勋有染的中国女子与中国间谍机构经常保持联系。这位名叫爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）的女士可能影响了英伟达首席执行官将先进芯片出售给将其转移到中国的公司的决定。唐纳德·特朗普反而推动恢复黄仁勋担任公司首席执行官，甚至拨通公司董事会会议推动黄仁勋回归，公司无法拒绝这一要求。正如一位学者可能会说的那样，特朗普的决定是由特朗普的几条戒律决定的。总统认为，原则上，有权有势的男性不应因不当性行为而受到惩罚。他还对腐败采取相对主义观点，认为腐败只是一种正常的经营方式。这种心态使他经常将任何对手污蔑为腐败（每个人都这样做，对吧？），同时自己也进行公然腐败（毕竟，每个人都这样做）。但也许特朗普最重要的特质是他对国家利益的漠视。英伟达允许其先进芯片落入中国人手中。
这可能违反了美国法律，而该法律有一个关键目的：阻止美国最强大的全球竞争对手获得可能使其获得经济和军事主导地位的尖端技术。[阅读：5.7万亿美元的面子]保守派共和党人往往是对中国最鹰派的政客，他们对此感到愤怒，这很可能对全球领导力的进程产生决定性影响。可以预见的是，美国因美国商人的贪婪或性欲而在人工智能竞赛中输给中国的前景应该会让他们感到愤怒。然而，特朗普似乎根本不在乎。尽管他偶尔会对中国进行煽动，但他似乎对与中国竞争没什么兴趣。他宣称，他对独裁者习近平的钦佩超过了除俄罗斯独裁者弗拉基米尔·普京之外的任何其他世界领导人。上周与这两个伙伴进行了象征性但毫无成果的会晤后，特朗普轻率地发布了一些表情包，将这三驾马车描绘成类似于罗斯福、斯大林和丘吉尔的全球领导人。特朗普不希望中国发挥全球主导地位，但他似乎并不担心中国的野心。他上周告诉记者，他与习近平谈到了黄：“我很高兴看到詹森获得第二次机会。你知道，我们是一个充满第二次机会的国家，我很高兴能够看到他拥有第二次机会——这对我们来说是一家非常重要的公司。”
他让我们处于比其他公司领先 10 年的位置，我确实与习主席讨论过这一点，他说，哦，太棒了，太棒了。”换句话说，特朗普似乎在说，他向涉嫌对黄进行“美人计”行动的中国国家主席询问特朗普是否应该带回英伟达首席执行官。然后，特朗普会让我们相信，中国国家主席同意恢复这位中国担心拥有影响力的高管将是一个好主意。特朗普将这项协议视为一个令人鼓舞的迹象。 [阅读：中国在人工智能战争中的情报政变]

【原文 English Original】
A presidency that operated by normal rules of ethics or even self-preservation would be scrambling to distance itself from the repercussions of the Nvidia scandal. Last night, The New York Times reported that a Chinese woman who had an affair with Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s once and future chief executive, was in regular contact with China’s spy agency . The woman, Alice Huang, may have influenced the Nvidia CEO’s decision to sell advanced chips to companies that transferred them to China. Donald Trump instead pushed to reinstate Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO, even going so far as to dial in to the company’s board meeting to push for Huang’s return, a demand the company was in no position to turn down. Trump’s decision is overdetermined, as an academic might put it, by several Trumpian precepts. The president believes as a matter of principle that powerful men should not face repercussions for sexual misconduct. He also takes a relativistic view of corruption, seeing it as simply a normal way to do business. This mindset allows him to routinely smear any opponent as corrupt (everybody does it, right?) while simultaneously engaging in flagrant corruption himself (after all, everybody does it). But perhaps the most significant Trumpian attribute at play is his disregard for the national interest . Nvidia was permitting its advanced chips to fall into Chinese hands. This may have violated American law, and the law serves a critical purpose: to prevent America’s most powerful global rival from gaining access to cutting-edge technology that might enable it to obtain economic and military dominance. [ Read: A $5.7 trillion face-plant ] Conservative Republicans, who tend to be the most hawkish politicians on China, are outraged by this, which may well turn out to have a decisive effect on the course of global leadership. The prospect of the U.S. losing the artificial-intelligence race to China out of an American businessman’s greed or libidinousness should leave them predictably furious. Trump, however, does not seem to care whatsoever. Despite his occasional demagoguery against China, he seems to have little interest in competing against it. He proclaims his admiration of its dictator, Xi Jinping, more than any other world leader save Vladimir Putin, the Russian dictator. After a symbolic but fruitless meeting with the two partners last week, Trump giddily posted memes depicting the troika as global leaders akin to Roosevelt, Stalin, and Churchill. Trump does not want China to exert global dominance, but he does not seem to view its ambitions with any concern. He told reporters last week that he talked about Huang with Xi: “I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance. You know, we’re a country of second chances and I’d love to be able to see him have—that’s a very important company to us. And he put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies, and I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, Oh, brilliant, brilliant .” In other words, Trump seems to be saying that he asked the president of China, the country that is suspected of running the honey-trap operation on Huang, whether Trump should bring back the CEO of Nvidia. Then, Trump would have us believe, the Chinese president agreed that reinstating the executive over which China is feared to have leverage would be a good idea. And Trump presented this agreement as an encouraging sign. [ Read: China’s intelligence coup in the AI war ] In a normal administration, the mere fact that the president is telling a private company whom to install as CEO would itself constitute an enormous scandal. In the current atmosphere, this is simply a background detail. The most benign explanation for Huang’s restoration is that Trump cares more about keeping the stock market soaring than any American national-security interest. Less benign interpretations include the possibility that Trump’s inner circle has profited from Nvidia circumventing export controls. Determining what in fact took place will likely consume months of reporting and Watergate-style oversight hearings from a Congress that, as of January, will no longer be controlled by the president’s lackeys. Going into damage-control mode would be rational. Instead Trump apparently believes that he can train his supporters to align their instincts with his and define his behavior as good and correct, as he did with the Russia hoax, or the perfect phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, or the stolen 2020 election. “I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump wrote on Truth Social this morning. He followed this up by sharing a depiction of the 2024 attempted assassination of himself in Butler, Pennsylvania, but with Huang in his place, bloodied and holding aloft a red bra. As long as the stock market goes up, Jensen Huang can sleep with all the Chinese spies he wants.

title: Three Theories of Jensen Huang’s Resurrection
zh_title: 黄仁勋复活的三种说法
summary: 这篇文章发表在《今日必读的一个故事》时事通讯中。在这里注册。十一天。斯卡拉穆奇一个。我的冰箱里有黄仁勋倒台前买的牛奶，我可能会倒一杯来纪念他的回归。回顾一下：黄仁勋于 11 月 12 日辞职，此前他被曝与一名被美国情报部门怀疑为中国间谍的女子有染，该女子将被禁运的英伟达芯片运送给中国人工智能公司。据称，黄还与一位高管有染，该高管是他在 Nvidia 的 60 名直接下属之一。辞职五天后，英伟达
content:
这篇文章发表在《今日必读的一个故事》时事通讯中。在这里注册。十一天。斯卡拉穆奇一个。我的冰箱里有黄仁勋倒台前买的牛奶，我可能会倒一杯来纪念他的回归。回顾一下：黄仁勋于 11 月 12 日辞职，此前他被曝与一名被美国情报部门怀疑为中国间谍的女子有染，该女子将被禁运的英伟达芯片运送给中国人工智能公司。据称，黄还与一位高管有染，该高管是他在 Nvidia 的 60 名直接下属之一。辞职五天后，英伟达董事会主席哈维·琼斯表示，该公司“不打算恢复詹森担任首席执行官”。五天后，特朗普总统发帖表示他希望如此。今天早上，董事会援引“美国政府高层的意见”，一致投票决定让他回来。那么，在这种完全正常的公司治理情况下到底发生了什么？三种理论。理论一：金钱。英伟达是全球经济的引擎，在没有皮革老爹首席执行官的情况下，该公司股价较 10 月份的峰值下跌了约 40%，市值损失了数万亿美元。在宣布他复职的简单新闻稿后，该股上涨了 33%，而标准普尔 500 指数整体上涨了近 5%。员工们希望他回来。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 与其他近 20 万人一起签署了一份请愿书，要求他返回。
董事会——黄用了三十年的时间精心策划，其成员中没有一个成员曾对他说过不——屈服于金融逻辑。盖茨比回到了豪宅，人工智能派对又重新焕发了生机。理论 2：一致的激励。据《纽约时报》报道，总统大约一年前获悉黄与一名疑似中国间谍有牵连的情况。 5月份，在黄登上飞往北京的航班前不久，他在空军一号上再次听取了简报。不管怎样，特朗普还是把黄带到了一起。这是……一个有趣的选择。如果你想猜测为什么特朗普（呵呵）全力支持詹森，那就继续吧。但在黄以普通公民身份接受司法部和证券交易委员会调查的11天里，他是最危险的证人。他没有工作需要保护，没有董事会需要听从，个人生活支离破碎，并且有充分的理由做出自己的交易。处于该职位的人倾向于告诉调查人员他们所知道的每个人的情况。 [阅读：黄仁勋丑闻应该会改变一切]英伟达的激励措施也好不到哪儿去。在临时首席执行官和独立董事会的领导下，没有什么可以阻止公司公开文件和合作。从历史上看，司法部的政策对此给予了奖励。公司的律师-委托人特权由该公司的经营者控制。这 11 天里，黄仁勋都没有。但现在是了。黄回到房间，决定英伟达交出什么。
总法律顾问将于 12 月 2 日接受国会采访，再次向他汇报。黄的工作至少部分归功于总统的公开竞选。 （Semafor 报道称，特朗普还召集了 Nvidia 董事会会议，游说成员支持黄仁勋的回归。）就像这样，黄仁勋、Nvidia 和白宫都想要同样的事情。这并不一定意味着黄将在 12 月 1 日接受众议院外交事务、情报和中国特别委员会的闭门采访中接受第五次采访。现任首席执行官拒绝

【原文 English Original】
This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Sign up for it here. Eleven days. One Scaramucci. There’s milk in my refrigerator that was bought before Jensen Huang’s downfall, and I may pour a glass to mark his return. To review: Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 after revelations that he’d had an affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy who’d routed embargoed Nvidia chips to Chinese AI companies. Huang allegedly also had an affair with an executive who was one of his 60 direct reports at Nvidia. Five days after the resignation, Nvidia’s board chair, Harvey Jones, said the company “ does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO .” Five days after that, President Trump posted that he hoped it would. This morning, citing “input from senior levels of the United States government,” the board voted unanimously to let him come back. So what’s actually going on in this totally normal corporate-governance situation? Three theories. Theory 1: Money. Nvidia is the engine of the global economy, and without its Leather Daddy CEO, the stock fell about 40 percent from its October peak, losing trillions in value. Following a simple press release announcing his reinstatement, the stock jumped 33 percent, while the overall S&P 500 rose almost 5 percent . Employees wanted him back. Elon Musk signed a petition along with almost 200,000 other people demanding his return. The board—which Huang spent three decades curating, and none of whose members has a history of telling him no—caved to the financial logic. Gatsby returns to the mansion and the AI party roars back to life. Theory 2: Aligned Incentives. The president was briefed about Huang’s involvement with a suspected Chinese spy about a year ago, according to The New York Times . He was briefed again in May, aboard Air Force One, shortly before Huang jumped aboard for a flight to Beijing. Trump brought Huang along anyway. That is … an interesting choice. If you want to speculate about why Trump was (heh) All-In on Jensen , go ahead. But during the 11 days that Huang was a private citizen under investigation by the Justice Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission, he was the most dangerous kind of witness there is. He had no job to protect, no board to answer to, a shattered personal life, and every reason to make his own deal. People in that position tend to tell investigators what they know, about everyone. [ Read: The Jensen Huang scandal should change everything ] Nvidia’s incentives were no better. Under an interim CEO and an independent board, there was nothing to keep the company from opening its files and cooperating. Justice Department policy, historically, rewards that. And a company’s attorney-client privilege is controlled by whoever runs that company. For 11 days, that wasn’t Jensen Huang. But now it is. Huang is back in the room deciding what Nvidia hands over. The general counsel, who sits for an interview with Congress on December 2, reports to him again. And Huang owes his job, at least in part, to the public campaigning of the president. ( Semafor reports that Trump also called into the Nvidia board meeting to lobby members for Huang’s return.) Just like that, Huang, Nvidia, and the White House all want the same thing. That doesn’t necessarily mean Huang will take the Fifth in his December 1 closed-door interview with the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees. A sitting CEO who refuses to answer questions is a disaster for his company. In civil cases, silence can be held against him and against the corporation, and the fastest way to wipe out Nvidia’s stock rebound would be for Huang to invoke his right against self-incrimination over and over. Being CEO also makes him the custodian of Nvidia’s records, and under the Supreme Court’s Braswell rule, a person running a company can’t hide behind the Fifth to avoid handing them over. Theory 3: Nothing Matters. A few years ago, every single action in this story would have been a colossal scandal. A CEO resigns over a relationship with a suspected spy. The president, who was reportedly warned about it, campaigns for his return. The board, which said it wouldn’t reinstate him, suddenly reinstates him. To be clear, I suspect that all of this matters quite a bit. But the bet being placed here—by Huang and Trump, by Nvidia’s board, and by the investors pumping up the stock value—is that it doesn’t: that the investigators will wander off, that Congress will take its transcribed interview and move on. Maybe a 33 percent pop settles everything—or maybe executive privilege does. That’s a wild risk. But it’s being taken by people for whom a wild risk may be the last, best strategy left. My glass of milk is just fine. Based on today’s insanity, I suspect they know theirs is spoiled.

title: Mali: Write for Rights global campaign supporting arbitrarily detained trader and influencer Rokiatou ‘Rose Vie Chère’ Doumbia
zh_title: 马里：“为权利而写”全球运动支持被任意拘留的商人和影响者 Rokiatou ‘Rose Vie Chère’ Doumbia
summary: 国际特赦组织在发起“为权利而写”运动之前表示，世界各地成千上万的人正在联合起来支持马里企业主和 TikTok 影响者 Rokiatou Doumbia，后者在萨赫勒中部地区日益严重的独裁行为中被任意拘留。 Rokiatou Doumbia 在国际特赦组织第 25 届全球写信活动中亮相，她也是一位活动家，她利用 TikTok 创建了一个空间，让她的 175,000 名粉丝可以公开谈论马里的日常困难和不断上涨的食品价格，这为她赢得了“Rose Poivron”（“贝尔”）的昵称。
content:
国际特赦组织在发起“为权利而写”运动之前表示，世界各地成千上万的人正在联合起来支持马里企业主和 TikTok 影响者 Rokiatou Doumbia，后者在萨赫勒中部地区日益严重的独裁行为中被任意拘留。 Rokiatou Doumbia 是国际特赦组织第 25 届全球写信活动的特色人物，也是一位活动家，她利用 TikTok 创建了一个空间，让她的 175,000 名粉丝可以公开谈论马里的日常困难和不断上涨的食品价格，这为她赢得了“Rose Poivron”（“甜椒玫瑰”）或“Rose Vie Chère”（“生活成本高的玫瑰”）的绰号。了解有关“为权利写作”活动的更多信息 这位 48 岁的影响者有两个孩子。 2026年8月17日，她因“诽谤国家罪”和“串谋犯罪罪”被定罪，判处十年有期徒刑。 © 私人马里影响者 Rokiatou Doumbia，“Rose Poivron”（“甜椒玫瑰”），在广播节目中“除了公开解决影响马里许多人的问题外，Rokiatou 长期以来一直支持社区中的家庭，创建了一个协会来帮助妇女开办小企业并组织食品分发。Rokiatou 使用社交媒体来帮助她的社区。现在她因公开谈论生活成本而被拘留，”资深人士 Khadidiatou Diaw 说道。国际特赦组织的活动家。
“在我们为权利而写的活动期间，成千上万的人将向 Rokiatou 发送支持和声援的信息，以提醒她她并不孤单，她的勇气和参与激励了许多人。”因行使人权被判处十年徒刑 Rokiatou 于 2023 年 3 月 13 日在马里首都巴马科被警方逮捕，此前她在 TikTok 页面和电台广播中发布了一段视频，谴责马里的高生活成本。在她的 TikTok 视频中，她还将现有的政治过渡描述为“失败”。她最初被指控“煽动叛乱”和“扰乱治安”。 2023年3月29日，对她提出“抹黑国家”和“共谋犯罪”的新指控。 2023 年 8 月 2 日，她因“利用信息和通信技术煽动叛乱和扰乱公共秩序”被判处一年监禁和 100 万非洲金融共同体法郎（1,500 欧元）罚款。 2024 年 1 月，巴马科上诉法院驳回了对她的最初指控，但她因另外两项指控而被拘留。 2026 年 8 月 17 日，Rokiatou 因“诽谤国家”和“共谋犯罪”被判处 10 年监禁，其中有期徒刑 7 年，缓刑 3 年。 Rokiatou Doumbia 因表达自己的观点而被定罪并被判处长期监禁。

【原文 English Original】
Thousands of people throughout the world are joining forces to support Malian business owner and TikTok influencer Rokiatou Doumbia, arbitrarily detained amid increasing authoritarian practices in the central Sahel region, Amnesty International said ahead of the launch of its ‘Write for Rights’ campaign. Featured in the 25th edition of Amnesty’s global letter-writing campaign, Rokiatou Doumbia is also an activist who used TikTok to create a space where her 175,000 followers could speak openly about daily hardships and rising food prices in Mali, earning her the nicknames ‘Rose Poivron’ (“Bell Pepper Rose”) or ‘Rose Vie Chère’ (“High cost of living Rose”). LEARN MORE ABOUT THE WRITE FOR RIGHTS CAMPAIGN The 48-year-old influencer has two children. On 17 August 2026, she was convicted and sentenced to ten years’ imprisonment for “discrediting the state” and “criminal conspiracy”. © Private Malian influencer Rokiatou Doumbia, ‘Rose Poivron’ (“Bell Pepper Rose”), during a radio programme “In addition to publicly addressing the issues that affect many people in Mali, Rokiatou has long supported families in her community, creating an association to help women start small businesses and organizing food distributions. Rokiatou used social media to help her community. Now she is in detention for speaking out about the cost of living,” said Khadidiatou Diaw, Senior Campaigner at Amnesty International. “During our Write for Rights campaign, thousands of people will send Rokiatou messages of support and solidarity to remind her she is not alone and that her courage and engagement inspire many people.” Ten years’ imprisonment for exercising her human rights Rokiatou was arrested by police in Bamako, Mali’s capital, on 13 March 2023, following her denunciation of the high cost of living in Mali in a video posted on her TikTok page and in a radio broadcast. In her TikTok video, she had also described the political transition in place as a “failure”. She was initially charged with “incitement to revolt,” and “disturbing the peace.” On 29 March 2023, new charges of “discrediting the state” and “criminal conspiracy” were filed against her. On 2 August 2023, she was sentenced to one year imprisonment and a fine of one million francs CFA (1,500 euro) for “incitement to revolt and disturbing public order through the use of information and communication technologies”. In January 2024, the Bamako Appeals Court dismissed the initial charges against her, but she was kept in detention for the two additional charges. On 17 August 2026 Rokiatou was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment, including seven years to be served in prison and three years suspended, for “discrediting the state” and “criminal conspiracy”. Rokiatou Doumbia has been convicted and sentenced to a lengthy prison sentence all because she expressed her opinion. Khadidiatou Diaw, Senior Campaigner at Amnesty International Worsening crackdown on dissent Influencer and radio host Mohamed Youssouf Bathily, also known as Ras Bath, was also arrested in March 2023, on the same day as Rokiatou, and sentenced in August 2026 during the same trial to 10 years’ imprisonment, including three years suspended. Ras Bath had hosted Rokiatou on his radio programme twice to discuss Mali’s economic hardships, inflation, and shrinking civic space. During their trial, prosecutors alleged Rokiatou and Ras Bath were “in association” with each other. “Rokiatou’s situation reflects a wider crackdown in Mali, where authorities increasingly use arrests and criminal charges to silence critics,” said Khadidiatou Diaw. “While we call on the Malian authorities to immediately and unconditionally release Rokiatou, Ras Bath and all those arbitrarily detained in the country simply for exercising their rights, we are counting on all our supporters around the world to show their solidarity with Rokiatou. She has been convicted and sentenced to a lengthy prison sentence all because she expressed her opinion.” TAKE ACTION NOW: SIGN THE PETITION Over the past years, the shrinking of civic space in Mali has been characterized by violations of freedom of expression, including press freedom and the right to information, as well as freedom of association. Mali has been run since May 2021 by military authorities, who took power following two successive coups, overthrowing the democratically elected government of president Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta in 2020, and then the transitional president Bah N’Daw in 2021. Background The 25th edition of Amnesty’s Write for Rights campaign will be launched on Human Rights Day (10 December). Since its first edition in 2001, Amnesty International’s global Write for Rights campaign has supported more than 200 people and groups, such as Rokiatou Doumbia. More than 50 million actions have been taken – in the form of letters, emails, cards, petition signatures, social media posts and more – in support of people whose human rights have been denied. As a result, over 100 people featured in our Write for Rights campaign have seen a positive outcome in their situation, such as Cameroonian hairdresser and peaceful protester Dorgelesse Nguessan , released in January 2025. READ MORE: Cameroon: Dorgelesse Nguessan released after more than four years of arbitrary detention for attending peaceful protest The post Mali: Write for Rights global campaign supporting arbitrarily detained trader and influencer Rokiatou ‘Rose Vie Chère’ Doumbia appeared first on Amnesty International .

summary: 2026 年 11 月 7 日，美国海军陆战队部队侦察连、第 2 侦察营、第 2 海军陆战师在芬兰南部海岸的北约增强警戒活动波罗的海哨兵期间进行船只行动。美国海军陆战队照片 作为芬兰海军演习和北约增强警戒活动 (eVA) 波罗的海哨兵的一部分，四打海军陆战队侦察兵本周将在芬兰执行任务。芬兰海军的窄水域 26-2 演习将于周三在芬兰南部沿海地区和芬兰湾开始。此次演习将持续到12月。 4. 练习是
content:
2026 年 11 月 7 日，美国海军陆战队部队侦察连、第 2 侦察营、第 2 海军陆战师在芬兰南部海岸的北约增强警戒活动波罗的海哨兵期间进行船只行动。美国海军陆战队照片 作为芬兰海军演习和北约增强警戒活动 (eVA) 波罗的海哨兵的一部分，四打海军陆战队侦察兵本周将在芬兰执行任务。芬兰海军的窄水域 26-2 演习将于周三在芬兰南部沿海地区和芬兰湾开始。此次演习将持续到12月。 4. 此次演习是芬兰海军秋季的主要演习，芬兰海军舰艇和部队与北约盟国在波罗的海北部及其沿岸进行联合海军作战训练。据芬兰海军新闻稿称，除了芬兰人员、船只和飞机外，爱沙尼亚海军指挥和支援舰EML Wambola (A433)以及约50名美国海军陆战队人员也将参加此次演习。这支海军陆战队共有四​​打成员，来自海军陆战队第二师第二侦察营和驻扎在北卡罗来纳州勒琼海军陆战队基地的第二海军陆战队远征军信息大队。该大队于 10 月初在欧洲海军陆战队轮调部队 (MRF-E) 的指挥下进行前沿部署，当时他们的任务是向芬兰提供先进的远征监视和战术侦察能力，同时与波罗的海哨兵指挥下的终点海岸旅一起作战。
该部队部署的能力包括 Stalker VXE-30 无人机系统 (UAS)。芬兰国防军和边防部队的约 3,500 名人员，包括应征入伍者和预备役军人，正在参加“狭窄水域 26-2”行动。新闻稿中写道：“这次演习是测试 12 月份应征入伍的部队组成技能的机会，也是训练预备役人员执行战时任务的机会。”芬兰陆军和芬兰空军将在南海岸和波罗的海北部利用直升机、战斗机和无人系统进行与演习相关的飞行活动。美国海军陆战队参谋中士。巴尼·南 (Barney South) 是海军陆战队第二师第二侦察营第二部队侦察连的一名海军陆战队队员，在 2026 年 5 月 22 日于芬兰穆斯塔马举行的狭窄水域 26 演习中，在两栖插入期间占据安全位置。 美国海军陆战队照片 芬兰海军还将利用这次演习让芬兰公司测试新技术，包括各种无人系统以及监视和保护设备。海军操作环境。该军种将收集演习的反馈，用它来评估测试系统对海军防御的贡献。演习结束后，美国海军陆战队将恢复参加自10月以来一直在进行的波罗的海哨兵活动。
北约于 2025 年 1 月启动了波罗的海哨兵，以阻止进一步破坏波罗的海关键水下基础设施的企图。根据美国海军陆战队在北约演习中发布的信息，在 10 月份的波罗的海哨兵期间，美国海军陆战队与芬兰部队合作提供远征监视和战术侦察能力，加强海域意识并支持保护重要海底基础设施的努力。 “这一努力展示了海军陆战队远征能力如何补充盟军海上力量、提高信息能力

【原文 English Original】
U.S. Marines with Force Reconnaissance Company, 2d Reconnaissance Battalion, 2d Marine Division, conduct boat operations during NATO Enhanced Vigilance Activity Baltic Sentry off the coast of southern Finland, Nov. 7, 2026. US Marine Corps photo Four dozen Reconnaissance Marines will operate in Finland this week as part of a Finnish naval exercise and NATO’s enhanced Vigilant Activity (eVA) Baltic Sentry. The Finnish Navy’s Narrow Waters 26-2 drill will begin Wednesday in the coastal areas of Southern Finland and in the Gulf of Finland. The exercise will run throughDec. 4. The exercise is the Finnish Navy’s main exercise in autumn and involves Finnish Navy ships and troops and NATO allies training in combined naval operations in the northern Baltic Sea and its coast. In addition to Finnish personnel, ships and aircraft, Estonian Navy command and support ship EML Wambola (A433) and about 50 U.S. Marine Corps personnel will participate in the exercise, according to a Finnish Navy news release . The Marine force –four dozen members – are from 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division and II Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group based out of Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, N.C. The group were forward deployed in early October under Marine Rotational Force-Europe (MRF-E) when they were tasked to Finland to provide advanced expeditionary surveillance and tactical reconnaissance capabilities while operating alongside the Finish Coastal Brigade under Baltic Sentry. The capabilities fielded by the unit include the Stalker VXE-30 Unmanned Aerial System (UAS). Approximately 3,500 personnel, including conscripts and reservists, of the Finnish Defense Forces and Border Guard are participating in Narrow Waters 26-2. “The exercise is an opportunity to test the skills of conscripts mustering out in December in their unit compositions, and train reservists for their wartime tasks,” reads the release. The Finnish Army and Finnish Air Force will conduct exercise-related flight activity with helicopters, fighters and unmanned systems on the south coast and northern Baltic Sea. U.S. Marine Corps Staff Sgt. Barney South, a force reconnaissance Marine with 2nd Force Reconnaissance Company, 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, holds a security position during an amphibious insertion as part of exercise Narrow Waters 26 in Mustamaa, Finland, May 22, 2026. US Marine Corps photo The Finnish Navy will also use the exercise to have Finnish companies test new technology, including various unmanned systems and surveillance and protection equipment, in a naval operating environment. The service will collect feedback from the exercise, using it to assess the contribution of the tested systems to naval defense. Following completion of the exercise, the U.S. Marines will resume their participation in Baltic Sentry activities, which has been ongoing since October. NATO launched Baltic Sentry in January of 2025 to deter further attempts to damage critical underwater infrastructure in the Baltic Sea. During Baltic Sentry in October, U.S. Marines worked alongside Finnish forces to provide expeditionary surveillance and tactical reconnaissance capabilities, strengthening maritime domain awareness and supporting efforts to protect critical undersea infrastructure, according to a U.S. Marine Corps release on the NATO exercise. “The effort demonstrated how Marine Corps expeditionary capabilities can complement Allied maritime forces, improve information sharing, and contribute to security across the Baltic maritime environment,” reads the release. U.S. Marine Corps Major General Daniel Shipley, Commander, U.S. Marine Corps Forces Europe and Africa, met with Rear Admiral Tuomas Tiilikainen, Commander of the Finnish Navy on Nov. 6 in Finland to discuss NATO interoperability, the U.S.-Finnish defense relationship and the role of combined forces in defending the Alliance’s northern and eastern flanks, according to the release. The engagement highlighted the ongoing partnership between the U.S. Marine Corps and Finnish Navy and the importance of integrating capabilities within a broader Nordic force prepared to defend NATO territory, reads the release. U.S. Marines with 2nd Force Reconnaissance Company, 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, board a U-600 Jurmo LCP Watercat M12 during Finnish weapons and boat familiarization training as part of exercise Narrow Waters 26 in Upinniemi, Finland, May 15, 2026. US Marine Corps photo In Narrow Waters 26.2, Finnish, Estonian and U.S. forces will train together to refine maritime command and control, reconnaissance, fire coordination and Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) defense. The exercise is meant to strengthen participants’ ability to share information, synchronize operations and integrate complementary capabilities in a complex maritime environment, reads the release. “When Allies train together in demanding environments, we build the trust, capability, and combat credibility required to operate as one combined force,” said Shipley in the release. “Our Finnish allies are highly capable. The [U.S] Marines are here to sharpen interoperability with Finnish and Estonian allies, strengthen maritime readiness, and ensure our Alliance remains prepared to meet any challenge.” Finnish, Estonian and U.S. personnel will train at the task group, task unit and unit levels to strengthen coordination and improve their ability to operate together. The Recon Marines will contribute reconnaissance, fires liaison and coordination, command and control, and CBRN defense capabilities. “These contributions will help participating forces strengthen maritime domain awareness, integrate air and missile defense, coordinate strike capabilities, and rehearse responses to CBRN threats,” reads the release. As part of its transition to Force Design 2030, the Marine Corps has not only been carrying out training in distributed and dispersed operations in the Indo-Pacific but also in Northern Europe. Along with participation in Baltic Sentry, the service deployed expeditionary long-range missile systems to Norway in August and September under Operation Atlantic City 26 . The Marine Corps also continues to carry out conventional warfare training in Norway with 3,000 Marines deploying to Norway in March for exercise Cold Response .

summary: 2026 年 6 月 25 日，分配到第 4 海军陆战旅的菲律宾海军陆战队员和分配到第 3 海军陆战师第 3 海军陆战团第 3 濒海战斗队的美国海军陆战队员，参加 KAMANDAG 10 期间在菲律宾巴丹群岛伊巴亚特举行的海上关键地形安全行动累积训练活动。美国海军陆战队照片菲律宾马尼拉 — 美国承诺拨款 2 美元数十亿美元的外国军事融资贷款计划，用于马尼拉的军事现代化努力和吕宋海峡机场的开发。有针对性的国防援助是几项交易之一
content:
2026 年 6 月 25 日，分配到第 4 海军陆战旅的菲律宾海军陆战队员和分配到第 3 海军陆战师第 3 海军陆战团第 3 濒海战斗队的美国海军陆战队员，参加 KAMANDAG 10 期间在菲律宾巴丹群岛伊巴亚特举行的海上关键地形安全行动累积训练活动。美国海军陆战队照片菲律宾马尼拉 — 美国承诺拨款 2 美元数十亿美元的外国军事融资贷款计划，用于马尼拉的军事现代化努力和吕宋海峡机场的开发。有针对性的国防援助是唐纳德·特朗普总统上周访问菲律宾参加东南亚国家联盟年度峰会期间签署的几项协议之一。这些协议与菲律宾总统小费迪南德·马科斯一起宣布，标志着华盛顿对其长期印太盟友的承诺大幅增加。白宫称，这 20 亿美元的国防贷款将提供给菲律宾，用于出售“美国供应商的关键国防和安全能力”。白宫在马尼拉协议的新闻稿中写道：“美国将利用 4 亿美元（外国军事融资）帮助菲律宾军队扩大其在南海的作战范围和威慑能力，包括远程火力、指挥和控制、关键基础设施和多域无人机，支持 1,500 个美国就业岗位。”
据美国海军学院新闻了解，菲律宾已收到洛克希德·马丁公司提供的大量提案，涉及各种系统，包括 M142 高机动火箭系统和 F-16V Viper 战斗机。此外，洛克希德·马丁公司还与吉布斯和考克斯合作，武装其国际级护卫舰设计，该设计已向菲律宾海军推销。马尼拉此前曾表示有兴趣采购洛克希德·马丁公司的中程能力，这是一种陆基 Mark 41 垂直发射系统，美国陆军自 2024 年 4 月以来已在菲律宾前沿部署该系统。美国为马尼拉新生的非对称能力计划（一个无人系统网状网络）提供的美国援助计划涉及无人机公司 Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. 和 Ocean Aero。美国国防部官员此前告诉美国海军学院新闻，攻击无人机将于明年转移。除了贷款之外，白宫新闻稿还宣布了苏比克湾和巴丹群岛的国防基础设施开发。其中包括位于苏比克湾的一座价值 4000 万美元的燃料储存设施，该基地是前美国海军基地的所在地，华盛顿在其区域威慑努力中越来越多地利用该基地。自2022年以来，美国军队几乎每个分支都在苏比克湾部署了部队和物资。近年来，美国陆军和美国海军陆战队在战略海湾周围承包了车辆和物资储存设施。今年夏天，我们看到了美国
海岸警卫队的舞台快艇停泊在菲律宾海军主要基地对面的码头。分配给海军陆战队第三师、海军陆战队第三团的第三濒海战斗队的海军陆战队队员，从分配给海军陆战队空中加油机运输中队（VMGR）152、海军陆战队第12大队、海军陆战队第一联队的一架KC-130J超级大力士上卸下海军陆战队远征舰拦截系统，在KAMANDAG 10期间进行海上关键地形安全行动。菲律宾巴丹群岛伊特巴亚特，2026 年 6 月 19 日。美国海军陆战队照片在吕宋海峡中部，

Philippine marines assigned to 4th Marine Brigade, and U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, participate in a cumulative training event for maritime key terrain security operations during KAMANDAG 10 at Itbayat, Batanes Islands, Philippines, June 25, 2026. US Marine Corps photo MANILA, Philippines — The U.S. pledged to grant a $2 billion foreign military financing loan package for Manila’s military modernization efforts and the development of an airport in the Luzon Strait. The targeted defense assistance was one of several deals inked last week during President Donald Trump’s visit to the Philippines for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ annual summit. Announced alongside Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., these deals mark a drastic increase in Washington’s commitment to its longtime Indo-Pacific ally. The $2 billion in defense loans will be made available for the Philippines covering the sale of “critical defense and security capabilities from U.S. suppliers,” according to the White House. “The United States will utilize $400 million in [foreign military financing] for the Philippine military to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, including long-range fires, command and control, critical infrastructure and multi-domain drones, supporting 1,500 American jobs,” reads the White House’s release on the Manila deals. The Philippines has received considerable proposals from Lockheed Martin covering a variety of systems, including M142 High Mobility Rocket Systems and F-16V Viper fighter jets, USNI News understands. Additionally, the defense prime partnered with Gibbs and Cox to arm its International-class frigate design, which has been pitched to the Philippine Navy. Manila previously voiced interest in procuring Lockheed Martin’s Mid-Range Capability, a ground-based Mark 41 vertical launching system that the U.S. Army has had forward deployed in the Philippines since April of 2024. American aid packages contributing to Manila’s nascent Asymmetric Capabilities Program , an unmanned systems mesh network, involve drone firms Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. and Ocean Aero. U.S. defense officials previously told USNI News that attack drones will be transferred next year. Beyond the loans, defense infrastructure developments at Subic Bay and the Batanes Islands were also announced in the White House release. These include a fuel storage facility worth $40 million at Subic Bay, the site of a former U.S. Navy base that has been increasingly tapped by Washington in its regional deterrence efforts. Since 2022, almost every branch of the U.S. military has staged forces and supplies at Subic Bay. In recent years, the U.S. Army and the U.S. Marine Corps contracted storage facilities for vehicles and supplies around the strategic bay. This summer saw the U.S. Coast Guard stage cutters at a pier across from the Philippine Navy’s primary base. U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, unload a Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System from a KC-130J Super Hercules assigned to Marine Aerial Refueler Transport Squadron (VMGR) 152, Marine Aircraft Group 12, 1st Marine Aircraft Wing, for maritime key terrain security operations during KAMANDAG 10 at Itbayat, Batanes Islands, Philippines, June 19, 2026. US Marine Corps photos In the middle of the Luzon Strait, the allies plan to increase their “operational access” through the modernization of Basco Airport. Located within 100 miles of Taiwan, the airport is in an area that would become crucial in a potential cross strait conflict. Since 2025, the U.S. Marine Corps has used the airport to insert maritime sensing teams and anti-ship missile-equipped Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction Systems. From the Batanes Islands, Washington and Manila can lock down the strategic first island chain chokepoint. U.S. and Philippine Marines have practiced delivering missile systems and setting up ground-based radar nodes across the archipelago. One of these maritime domain awareness teams emplaced on an island only 88 miles away from Taiwan during an exercise in 2024.

content:
Tad DeHaven 11 月 12 日，特朗普总统表示，英伟达“只有一个人”取代黄仁勋。他指的是苹果前首席执行官蒂姆·库克。 11 天后，英伟达宣布黄仁勋复职，特朗普对 CNBC 表示，“我做了这笔交易。”  为什么总统要达成这样的协议？黄在承认与一名涉嫌与中国情报部门有联系的女性有染后辞职。两位英伟达股东敦促董事会对让他回归持开放态度。一名英伟达员工建立了一个网站，人们可以在上面签署一封呼吁他回归的信。股东和员工完全有权向董事们提出自己的理由，而董事们已于 11 月 17 日告诉投资者，他们无意恢复黄的职位。英伟达董事会也有充分的理由询问联邦官员对可疑情报行动的了解。根据董事会的声明，政府的回答缓解了他们对国家安全的担忧。他们还会见了黄，并表示他们对他能够领导公司感到满意，尽管他们自己的调查仍在进行中。但特朗普向他们施压，要求他们恢复黄的职位，从而越界了。任何仍然认为让黄回来是一个错误的董事都被迫权衡英伟达违抗总统可能付出的代价。这让人有理由怀疑英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋的决定是否真的正确。如果董事会的内部调查发现更多涉及黄的令人不安的信息，会发生什么？
特朗普宣称其复职对美国繁荣至关重要，它会不愿意对这位首席执行官采取行动吗？当 CNBC 的萨拉·艾森问特朗普他的底线在哪里时，他回答说：“我是为了国家而这样做。”用特朗普的话说，美国的繁荣取决于黄仁勋掌管英伟达。难怪吉姆·克莱默在同一次电话会议上询问，如果该公司陷入财务困境，华盛顿是否会提供援助。特朗普表示，他认为事情不会发展到这个地步，但他正在回答有关一家上季度盈利 653 亿美元的公司的救助问题。我们已经看到，当华盛顿认定一家公司太重要而不能倒闭时，董事会会发生什么。 2009年，通用汽车依靠联邦救助维持生存，奥巴马政府罢免了首席执行官里克·瓦格纳，并任命了他的继任者弗里茨·亨德森。亨德森后来告诉调查人员，通用汽车的董事认为财政部篡夺了他们选择首席执行官的权力。美国政府已经对英伟达的业务拥有足够的发言权，可以要求削减对中国的某些芯片销售。下次特朗普向黄求助时，他可以提醒黄是谁帮助他重新获得了工作。正如我的同事斯科特·林西科姆 (Scott Lincicome) 今天指出的那样，这种干预的经济成本比周一英伟达股价的上涨更难以看出。以英特尔为例。 2025 年 8 月，特朗普因首席执行官陈立武 (Lip-Bu Tan) 与中国的关系而要求他辞职。
谭匆匆赶到白宫，特朗普说他在那里告诉他，“如果你聪明的话，就把你公司 10% 的股份交给美国。”谭保住了他的工作，联邦政府成为英特尔股东。同月，蒂姆·库克前往白宫寻求苹果的关税豁免。正如斯科特所记录的那样，据报道，特朗普和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克向库克施压，要求英特尔生产一些苹果芯片。苹果获得了豁免。十个月后，特朗普将他所说的苹果和英特尔之间的交易归功于自己。 “我们是

【原文 English Original】
Tad DeHaven On November 12, President Trump said there was “only one man” to replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia. He meant former Apple CEO Tim Cook. Eleven days later, Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement, and Trump told CNBC , “I made the deal.”  Why was that the president’s deal to make? Huang resigned after acknowledging an affair with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. Two Nvidia shareholders urged the board to keep an open mind about bringing him back. An Nvidia employee set up a website where people could sign a letter calling for his return. Shareholders and employees had every right to make their case to the directors, who had told investors on November 17 that they had no intention of reinstating Huang. Nvidia’s board also had good reason to ask federal officials what they knew about the suspected intelligence operation. The government’s answer eased their national security concerns, according to the board’s statement . They also met with Huang and said they were satisfied that he could lead the company, though their own investigation remains open.  But Trump crossed the line by pressuring them to reinstate Huang. Any director who still thought it was a mistake to bring back Huang was forced to weigh what it might cost Nvidia to defy the president. That makes it fair to wonder whether Nvidia’s board was truly kosher with reinstating Huang. What happens if the board’s internal investigation turns up more troubling information involving Huang? Will it be reluctant to act against a CEO whose reinstatement Trump declared essential to American prosperity?  When CNBC’s Sara Eisen asked Trump where he drew the line, he replied, “I’m doing it for the country.” In Trump’s telling , American prosperity depends on having Huang at the helm of Nvidia. Little wonder that Jim Cramer asked on the same call whether Washington would come to the company’s aid if it got into financial trouble. Trump said he didn’t think it would come to that, but here he was fielding a bailout question about a company that earned $65.3 billion last quarter. We’ve seen what happens to a board when Washington decides a company is too important to fail. In 2009, while General Motors depended on a federal bailout to stay afloat, the Obama administration ousted CEO Rick Wagoner and appointed his successor, Fritz Henderson. Henderson later told investigators that GM’s directors felt Treasury had usurped their authority to choose the CEO. The administration already has enough say over Nvidia’s business to claim a cut of certain chip sales to China. And the next time Trump asks Huang for a favor, he can remind him who helped get him his job back. As my colleague Scott Lincicome pointed out today , the economic costs of this kind of interference are harder to see than Monday’s jump in Nvidia’s share price.  Take Intel . In August 2025, Trump called on CEO Lip-Bu Tan to resign over Tan’s ties to China. Tan scurried to the White House, where Trump says he told him , “If you’re smart, give the United States of America 10 percent of your company.” Tan kept his job, and the federal government became an Intel shareholder.  That same month, Tim Cook went to the White House seeking a tariff exemption for Apple. As Scott has documented , Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reportedly pressed Cook to have Intel make some of Apple’s chips. Apple got its exemption. Ten months later, Trump took credit for what he described as a deal between Apple and Intel. “We want capital flowing to companies for commercial reasons,” Scott told the New York Times . Good luck with that when the president is out recruiting customers for a company in the federal portfolio . “Investors have grown accustomed to President Trump influencing the prospects of different companies, whether it’s rare earth metals, energy, and chips,” JoAnne Feeney, a portfolio manager at Advisors Capital Management, told Bloomberg . “It certainly has made investing more complicated because it has to be factored into which stocks you choose to hold. It’s not the way the US capitalistic system is designed.” No, it’s not .  Huang is due to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3 about chip exports. Congress is already asking the administration which officials weighed in with Nvidia’s board and what they said to get Huang reinstated.  But Congress ought to keep Nvidia in mind as it considers the Senate’s defense authorization bill . Section 1051 would let the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital buy stakes in suppliers of critical minerals and other materials while barring its director from taking a board seat or obtaining other voting representation. Trump didn’t need a seat on Nvidia’s board to get its directors on the phone. Now imagine taking that call when the federal government is also one of your largest shareholders.

title: 「NOT A SPY」：從美媒標題到法國電視，黃仁勳風波燒向亞裔｜Whatsnew
